column19: The PV installed capacity within the Municipality of Athens in September 2025 was 30.2 MVA and was retrieved from the database of the national grid operator DEDDIE (https://apps.deddie.gr/WebAPE/main.html). This estimation may also include PV capacity from neighbouring municipalities. It was then converted to MW assuming a power factor of 0.9 (27.18 MW) and, subsequently, to a 2023 estimation, assuming that the municipal PV installed capacity in 2023 was at the 56% of the 2025 capacity, as it was the case at a national level (https://newtransparency.entsoe.eu/generation/installed/perType?permalink=68c40fe52eef503ba75cfce2).This installed capacity (15.22 MW) is then converted to an estimation of annual generation using an average capacity factor of 17.9% generated from PVGIS of the EU JRC (https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/pvg_tools/en/).\n\n

column19: A Usina Hidrelétrica Chaminé possui capacidade instalada de 18 MW, e está localizada na margem esquerda do rio São João, no município de São José dos Pinhais, em área de preservação permanente na Serra do Mar, a 78 km de Curitiba. Foi o primeiro grande projeto hidrelétrico do Paraná e teve papel fundamental no desenvolvimento econômico e social de Curitiba. Foi construída pela Cia. Força e Luz do Paraná, sob a orientação do americano Howell Lewis Fry, começando a operar em 1930. Ao ser concluída, em 1931, permitiu a desativação da Usina Térmica do Capanema, que era movida a lenha. Foi incorporada pela Copel em 1975. Até hoje, Chaminé mantém-se funcional e tecnicamente engenhosa. Um destaque é o meio de transporte entre a vila residencial e a casa de força, realizado por um bondinho (trole) em atividade desde 1928. O percurso é de mais de 600 metros, vencendo planos praticamente verticais e declives de até 55 graus em aproximadamente 10 minutos. Em 1946 e 1952, Chaminé teve sua potência instalada ampliada com o acréscimo dos grupos 3 e 4. A Usina possui dois reservatórios: Barragem de Vossoroca, com função de acumulação, e Barragem de Salto do Meio, com função de regulação. Chaminé possui quatro unidades geradoras.

column19: The City of Ankara has not yet estimated the installed capacity or annual generation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems within the jurisdiction boundary in a systematic and city-wide manner. While small-scale rooftop solar projects and rural solar irrigation support exist, the absence of comprehensive monitoring and reporting prevents an official figure from being disclosed. However, Ankara Metropolitan Municipality is promoting renewable integration, particularly in rural agricultural services through solar irrigation support, and future updates of the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and the Green City Action Plan will provide more precise capacity and generation data. The lack of quantified PV data is not due to an absence of activity, but rather the fragmented and decentralized nature of installations, which require consolidated reporting.

column19: Data on installed capacity and generation from solar thermal systems (such as rooftop solar water heating) are not currently estimated at the jurisdiction-wide scale. Although solar water heating technology is present in Ankara, especially in residential and small commercial buildings, comprehensive data collection and official capacity assessment are not yet integrated into the municipal GHG inventory. Future inventories are planned to include estimates from solar thermal applications through household energy surveys, sectoral studies, and potential collaboration with energy service companies.

column19: Within the boundaries of Ankara, hydropower generation facilities exist at the regional level, but their contribution is not estimated separately at the jurisdiction-wide level. National electricity grid data already integrates hydropower as part of the overall mix, but city-specific capacity and generation data are not disaggregated. Ankara Metropolitan Municipality depends on national-level grid allocation for hydroelectric contribution, and no direct hydropower plants are managed by the city authority itself. As such, hydropower data is reported as “Not Estimated (NE)”.

column19: Wind energy installations are present within the broader province of Ankara, but their installed capacity and annual generation are not disaggregated specifically for the municipal boundary. While national data confirms the existence of operational wind farms in nearby districts, the city-level Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and GCoM reporting rely on consolidated provincial or national datasets. Municipal-scale monitoring systems are not yet in place to track the capacity or generation of wind energy specifically for the jurisdiction, and therefore this data remains “Not Estimated (NE)”.

column19: Biomass and biofuel energy production potential exists in Ankara, particularly through waste-to-energy processes and rural agricultural residues, but no systematic monitoring of installed capacity and annual generation data has been conducted. Municipal initiatives such as the closure of the Mamak solid waste facility and exploration of new waste-to-energy solutions underline the commitment to renewable bioenergy. However, the technical data required for official reporting in terms of installed MW and generated MWh are not available, and thus the entry remains “Not Estimated (NE)”.

While geothermal resources are often used for district heating and thermal applications in Turkey, Ankara Metropolitan Municipality has not developed dedicated geothermal projects at scale within its SECAP framework. Hence, geothermal is marked as “Not Estimated (NE)”.

column19: O painel público da ANEEL disponibiliza dados por município sobre a capacidade instalada, discriminados por tipo de tecnologia. Em Salvador, conforme a atualização mais recente, a capacidade instalada de geração distribuída totaliza 27.954,07 MW no ano de 2024, sendo composta majoritariamente por sistemas fotovoltaicos solares, que representam 100% do total. Adicionalmente, avaliamos o potencial de geração de energia renovável com base nessa capacidade instalada. Utilizando um fator de capacidade conservador de 18% para a energia solar fotovoltaica, estimamos uma geração anual de aproximadamente 44.077,98 MWh.

column19: A estimativa de 28,76 MWh por ano de geração a partir da fonte eólica em Salvador foi calculada com base na potência instalada registrada no município, de 8,2 kW, conforme dados da ANEEL. Para essa estimativa, considerou-se um fator de capacidade médio de 40%, valor comumente utilizado para usinas eólicas no Brasil. Esse fator representa a proporção do tempo em que o sistema opera efetivamente em sua capacidade total ao longo do ano. Aplicando esse parâmetro à potência instalada e ao número total de horas anuais, chega-se à estimativa de geração anual de 28,76 MWh, refletindo uma produção teórica compatível com as condições médias de operação dessa fonte no país. O dado corresponde à serie histórica completa. (2006 - 2025)

Sierra Leone enjoys sunshine for most of the year, giving solar energy the greatest potential to expand energy access nationwide. The country's average solar radiation is about 1,872 kWh/m², making it highly suitable for solar power generation.

The adoption of solar photovoltaic (PV) technology is steadily increasing, particularly through the development of mini-grids in rural communities. However, there are still substantial opportunities to power more communities with solar solutions.

The Renewable Energy Policy outlines the following objectives for the solar sub-sector:

Increase the contribution of solar energy to the national energy mix, targeting a minimum of 10% electricity supply in rural areas by 2020 and 20% by 2030.

Extend electricity access to rural, remote, and off-grid areas through solar home systems.

Expand the productive use of solar technologies — such as solar water heating — for social services, commercial activities, and industrial processes.

Sierra Leone's current installed electricity capacity is primarily based on hydropower, with the recent addition of heavy fuel oil (HFO) generation helping to reduce the impact of seasonal fluctuations in water levels and providing firm capacity to the grid. In addition, small diesel generators across various regions supply power through local transmission systems.

The country's main generation asset is the Bumbuna Hydropower Plant, which has an installed capacity of 50 MW, along with several smaller hydropower stations. Commissioned in 2009, Bumbuna is highly seasonal — operating at full capacity mainly during the rainy season.

The absence of comprehensive data can be primarily attributed to limitations in governmental reporting mechanisms. Unfortunately, there has been a significant lack of detailed and consistent data collection at the local and national levels, particularly concerning small-scale domestic production. In many cases, these smaller, decentralised systems, such as domestic solar energy production, are not sufficiently monitored or accounted for within broader city-wide or national energy statistics.

Moreover, the production in question is of a small-scale, decentralised nature, predominantly occurring at the domestic level. This form of production often escapes inclusion in larger datasets, as governmental bodies have not yet established adequate frameworks to track or integrate these contributions into official records. Consequently, despite its potential significance, this form of production remains largely unaccounted for, contributing to the data gaps we currently face.

column19:
Parque Solar “La Unión” (Montería, Córdoba)
Capacidad instalada: 100 MW fotovoltaicos. 

Generación estimada anual: Entre 160 000 y 200 000 MWh/año, según estándares genéricos para plantas solares de esa escala (~1.6-2.0 GWh/MW anual), lo que equivale a abastecer a más de 132 000 hogares.

Mini-granja solar institucional (hasta mediados de 2025)
•Capacidad instalada proyectada: ~3 MW fotovoltaicos, ubicada en el centro de bienestar animal “Huellas” 
•Generación anual estimada: Aproximadamente 4 800 MWh/año, considerando una productividad típica de ~1.6 GWh/MW (dependiendo de irradiación local), para consumo institucional.

Proyecto Sol y Cielo (En operación)
9,9 MW instalados

Notas importantes
•	La estimación de generación anual se basa en valores tipo para plantas solares fotovoltaicas en regiones tropicales (~1.6-2 GWh/MW/año), pero puede variar según irradiancia, mantenimiento y eficiencia.
•	El proyecto “La Unión” ya está operativo desde septiembre de 2024, con impacto real en la matriz energética local y regional.
•	No se identifican actualmente proyectos eólicos ni de biomasa en Montería, lo que indica que la ciudad por ahora depende exclusivamente de la solar como fuente renovable relevante.
•	Existen planes municipales para expansión de paneles solares en colegios rurales y sectores institucionales, lo cual incrementaría la capacidad distribuida en años próximos
Montería cuenta actualmente con ~103 MW de capacidad renovable instalada, proveniente totalmente de energía solar fotovoltaica, con una generación aproximada de ~165 000-205 000 MWh al año. No hay generación eólica ni biomásica operativa en el municipio. Las futuras expansiones locales se centran en proyectos de escala menor (solar distribuida), especialmente en instituciones públicas rurales.
